closed_decision.resolved: Completed rather than withdrawn. Recording it as an A/B choice between doing the work and dropping the coordinate was the wrong framing: the capacity was already approved, and finding the bound in more places is wiring to finish, not a decision to re-open.

two_distinct_causes.REPEATED_WITHIN_SCOPE: historical_text_results counts normalised block text within the scope and treats anything appearing more than once as page furniture. That rule was added to drop running headers and it does. It also drops a product sub-heading that legitimately appears twice in one note - Comirnaty appears under 'Actions in Which We are the Defendant' and again under 'Matters Involving Pfizer and its Collaboration/Licensing Partners'.
two_distinct_causes.SUBSTANTIVE_MINIMUM_LENGTH_12: text_business_candidates._substantive requires at least twelve characters. Product names are shorter than that: Zantac is six, Chantix seven, Paxlovid and Asbestos eight, Docetaxel nine. Orgovyx (relugolix) at nineteen is kept, so the set is inconsistent in a way that depends on how long the generic name is.

defects.shared_root_cause: The page-furniture criterion identifies a running header by repetition: a block that repeats inside its scope next to another repeating block. Enphase writes its footer as one block that carries the page number, so every instance is a different text and no two can be compared. This is not the scope-coverage problem fixed in the same reading - widening that criterion to every scope removes Ford's eight running headers and, measured over all eleven saved periods, touches nothing else, including this block.

defects.why_it_is_not_repaired: Catching it needs a second criterion - repetition after the digits are removed, or something like it - and this corpus offers exactly one example of it. A rule written from one filing is the rule that fails on the seventh, which is the mistake this Issue has already made and recorded. It is registered so the coordinate stops counting as verified, and a positive case is what would justify writing the rule.

purpose: Results this repository has confirmed hold wrong content. An entry withdraws a result from current delivery. It does not delete it, re-sign it, or relabel it as a structural non-applicability: the original Run stays readable so the defect can be demonstrated and the repair checked.
release_rule: A coordinate-level entry stops withdrawing only when its 'released' block names the repaired result by result_id, and the Requirement closure it was produced under. repair_state is a note about the work; it releases nothing. An entry naming a result_id withdraws exactly that result and is never released.
